description: Unauthorized Access to Training Data in S3 Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies, steal credentials, or take advantage of misconfigured bucket policies to access training data stored in S3. An attacker compromises a HyperPod node's IAM role or obtains temporary credentials, then uses these to download sensitive training data from the S3 bucket.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
mitreATT&CK: T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
recommendation: Implement S3 bucket key to reduce KMS costs and strengthen encryption
recommendation: Implement strict S3 bucket policy
recommendation: Enable S3 access logging and implement automated monitoring

description: EFS Shared Storage Race Conditions and Data Corruption Concurrent access to shared files on EFS by multiple HyperPod nodes without proper synchronization mechanisms could lead to data corruption or inconsistent states. During distributed training, multiple nodes attempt to write checkpoints simultaneously, causing corruption of model weights or loss of training progress.
references: recommendation: Monitor EFS metrics for potential issues

description: Insecure HTTPS Configuration on Load Balancer The current implementation has a placeholder HTTPS listener without proper certificate configuration, potentially allowing for weak cipher suites or vulnerable TLS versions. An attacker performs a MITM attack by exploiting weak TLS configuration or invalid certificates, intercepting sensitive data between users and the HPC cluster.
references: recommendation: Configure ACM certificate for HTTPS

description: Excessive IAM Permissions on HyperPod Instance Role The current implementation uses AWS managed policies which may provide more permissions than necessary for the HyperPod nodes to function. An attacker who compromises a HyperPod node could leverage the instance's IAM role to access other AWS services or escalate privileges.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
mitreATT&CK: T1548 - Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
recommendation: Create custom IAM policies with minimal permissions

description: Insufficient Network Segmentation and Security Group Rules Current security group configurations may allow broader network access than necessary, potentially enabling lateral movement or unauthorized access to services. An attacker who compromises one HyperPod node could potentially access other nodes or services due to overly permissive security group rules.
references: recommendation: Implement strict security group rules
